title: Working at Redwood — Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools Guide
author: Sofia Nguyen
body:
Overview

This page consolidates the core employee-facing policies and practical guidance for working at Redwood: role definitions and career ladders, benefits and perks, an overview of the hiring and onboarding process, and the set of internal tools new hires need to access. It is intended for new and existing employees and managers as a single reference to get started or answer common operational questions.

Contents:
1. Roles & career ladders
2. Benefits & perks summary
3. Hiring and onboarding overview
4. Internal tools and access guide
5. Manager responsibilities and 90-day milestones
6. Quick reference: people-ops contacts

---

## 1) Roles & career ladders

Short intro: Redwood uses structured ladders for Engineering, Product, Design and Customer-facing teams. Ladders differentiate between Individual Contributor (IC) and Manager paths and provide clear expectations across level, impact, scope, and leadership. Promotions are evidence-driven and executed quarterly.

Key concepts:
- Levels: L1 (new grad/entry) through L6+ (senior staff/principal).
- Dimensions evaluated: Product & customer impact, technical ownership, scope, cross-team influence, mentorship, and execution velocity.
- IC vs Manager: Promotion criteria for managers include people leadership, career development of direct reports, and org-level program delivery. IC criteria emphasize technical or product leadership and cross-functional influence.

Example summary table (engineer ladder):
| Level | Typical title(s) | Scope & impact | Promotion signals |
|-------|------------------|----------------|------------------|
| L2 | Software Engineer | Team feature delivery, writes production code | Consistent shipping, ownership of components |
| L3 | Senior Software Engineer | Cross-team projects, technical design | Leads designs, mentors peers, reliable delivery |
| L4 | Staff Engineer | Multi-team technical initiatives | Shapes roadmap, long-term architecture |

Promotion process (high level):
1. Candidate prepares a promotion packet with accomplishments + evidence mapped to ladder rubrics.
2. Manager reviews and submits to calibration panel.
3. Calibration panel collects feedback from reviewers and people-ops; decision recorded in HR system.
4. Outcome and development plan communicated to employee.

Where to find the full ladders and rubrics: See linked ladders in Confluence (Engineering ladder, Product ladder, Design ladder).

---

## 2) Benefits & perks (summary)

We offer a competitive benefits package designed to support health, family, and productivity. The People Ops team administers benefits; specific vendor links and plan documents are available in the Benefits portal.

Core offerings (high-level):
- Health insurance: Medical, dental, vision plans with company contribution.
- Retirement: 401(k) plan with employer match (details in benefits portal).
- Paid time off: 20 days PTO baseline (varies by country/role), national holidays, and flexible time off policy for exempt employees.
- Parental leave: Primary caregiver parental leave of up to 18 weeks; non-primary up to 12 weeks (policy varies by region and employment law).
- Paid family care & bereavement leave per policy.
- Flexible work & remote-first: Redwood supports hybrid and remote work; on-site expectations are set by teams.
- Stipends: Home office and learning & development stipend ($1,000/year by default), and conference budget for eligible roles.
- Perks: Commuter benefits (region-specific), monthly wellness stipend, employee assistance program (EAP), and quarterly hack days.

How to enroll / change plans:
- Enroll via the Benefits portal within 30 days of hire or during annual open enrollment.
- Contact benefits@redwood.example.com for manual enrollment issues.

---

## 3) Hiring & onboarding overview

Recruiting philosophy: Hire for long-term fit and potential. The process is engineered to be fast for candidates and equitable across roles.

Standard hiring flow:
1. Requisition and scorecard creation (Hiring manager + Recruiting partner)
2. Resume screen and recruiter outreach
3. Phone screen(s) (culture and role fit)
4. Technical/functional loop — typically 2–4 interviews (coding/design/system design/product sense)
5. Cross-functional interview(s) as needed (customer success, security, infra)
6. Final hiring committee / calibration (for senior roles)
7. Offer, background check, and closing

Offer & negotiation guidance for hiring managers:
- Follow the comp band guidance in the People Ops hiring toolkit.
- Escalate exception compensation to People Ops and Finance using the exception form.

New-hire onboarding timeline (90-day summary):
- Pre-boarding (before start date): accounts created, equipment ordered, welcome email with first-week agenda.
- Week 0–1: Orientation (company values, benefits overview), tooling setup, meet & greets, and first small deliverable.
- Month 1: Deeper product/stack training, assigned mentor, first project kickoff.
- Month 2: Ownership of a small feature or operational task, feedback checkpoint with manager.
- Month 3: Formal 90-day review (expectations review, early career development plan).

New-hire checklist (examples):
1. Complete employment paperwork and tax forms.
2. Sign up for benefits and payroll.
3. Complete security training and MFA setup.
4. Confirm GitHub/CI access and code of conduct acknowledgment.
5. Ensure Slack, Confluence, Jira access and linking to team channels.

First-week sample schedule (day-by-day):
- Day 1: Orientation, equipment validation, Slack intros, benefits briefing.
- Day 2: Product overview, meet core teammates, set up dev environment.
- Day 3: Training sessions (security & infra), small bug or doc task assigned.
- Day 4–5: Continue ramping, 1:1 with manager, social intro with cross-functional partners.

## 4) Internal tools and access guide

This section lists the primary internal tools, default owners, and common access procedures. If a tool you need is missing from this list, open a ticket with people-ops or your manager.

Primary tools and first steps:
- SSO / Okta: Primary identity provider. You will receive an Okta invite during pre-boarding. Use it to provision email, Slack, and other SAML apps.
- Google Workspace: Company email and docs. New hires are provisioned automatically; use the shared drive for team docs.
- Slack: Primary communication. Join #welcome and your team channel. Set your status and profile photo.
- Confluence: Internal documentation. All employees have read access; edit rights are granted by team space owners.
- GitHub (org: redwood-inference): Code repositories. Request membership and repo-level access through the access request form.
- Jira: Issue tracking. Team boards provisioned by platform; ask your manager if you need board admin rights.
- Zoom: Video conferencing with SSO.
- VPN / Bastion access: Required for some infra tasks. Request via infra-access ticket and complete network security training.
- Internal HR/People Ops portal: Benefits, payroll, and time-off requests.

How to request access (step-by-step):
1. Confirm the access you need with your manager and list required repos/boards/apps.
2. Open a ticket via the People Ops portal (link provided in your welcome email). Use the subject prefix: [Access Request].
3. People Ops and tool owners will approve and provision access within 1–3 business days (expedited for urgent needs).

Common command snippets and examples:
- GitHub: Request org membership via: https://github.com/orgs/redwood-inference/invitation
- VPN: Follow instructions in the infra runbook: /confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/vpn-setup (search from Confluence home).

Minimal security checks for access:
- MFA enabled in Okta (required).
- Completion of security awareness training (pre-req for VPN and high-privilege roles).

Quick access table:
| Tool | Owner | Typical SLA for access |
|------|-------|------------------------|
| Okta | People Ops | 0–1 business day
| GitHub org | Eng Platform | 1–3 business days
| Jira | Eng Platform | 1–2 business days
| Confluence | People Ops / space owners | 0–1 business day

## 5) Manager responsibilities & 90-day milestones

Managers should ensure a predictable ramp for new hires and run timely check-ins. Key responsibilities:
- Provide a clear plan for the first 90 days with measurable milestones.
- Assign a peer buddy and onboarding tasks.
- Conduct weekly 1:1s during the first month and bi-weekly thereafter.
- Complete the 30/60/90 feedback forms and submit to People Ops.

90-day milestone examples (for ICs):
- 30 days: Able to run the local dev environment and make a small production change.
- 60 days: Lead a small feature or bug fix end-to-end with minimal guidance.
- 90 days: Clear development plan and measurable impact on a team objective.
